nodes.description: Oral N-acetylcysteine (NAC) has been investigated in ACys/HCCAA, not established as a disease-modifying treatment. An open-label phase IIa study enrolled 17 CST3 L68Q carriers and administered 2400 mg daily for nine months. Plasma high-molecular-weight cystatin C and several skin fibrosis/cell-activation biomarkers decreased, but the reduction in skin cystatin C staining was not statistically significant (P=0.27). Five participants had cerebral bleeds during treatment. The small uncontrolled study, prior NAC use by nine participants and subjective biomarker scoring limit inference; prevention of hemorrhage, dementia or death and benefit in amyloid-beta CAA remain unproven.

evidence.snippet: In CAA, amyloid-β accumulation is detected primarily in the neocortical and leptomeningeal arterioles, and to a lesser extent in capillaries and venules [17,18].

evidence.reference_title: Main features of hereditary cerebral amyloid angiopathies: A systematic review.
evidence.snippet: Sporadic CAA is caused by deposition of amyloid-β (Aβ), originating from proteolytic cleavage of the Amyloid Precursor Protein (APP), within the walls of cerebral small caliber vessels.

evidence.reference_title: https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/10173198/1/Werring_Pathophysiological%20framework%20for%20CAA%20-%20FINAL.pdf
evidence.snippet: There is no evidence for substantial A overproduction in sporadic or Dutch-type hereditary CAA,23 suggesting that A deposition may instead reflect increased aggregation or impaired clearance.

nodes.description: Cystatin C amyloid deposits in cerebral vessel walls together with collagen IV-rich extracellular matrix. The basement-membrane lesion is associated with smooth-muscle degeneration; the relative causal roles of fibrosis and amyloid deposition remain under investigation.

evidence.reference_title: The historical background of hereditary cystatin C amyloid angiopathy: Genealogical, pathological, and clinical manifestations.
evidence.snippet: Cystatin C amyloid complex deposition begins in the basement membrane around SMA cells in the media of the vessel wall.

nodes.description: White matter hyperintensities, including a multispot pattern, are non-hemorrhagic MRI findings. The multispot pattern is one white-matter feature in the Boston criteria v2.0; it is distinct from enlarged perivascular spaces.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Management of Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy.
evidence.snippet: Visible enlarged perivascular spaces in the centrum semiovale detected in T2-weighted sequences and white matter hyperintensities in a multispot pattern detected in FLAIR sequences represent also common neuroimaging findings and were incorporated in the recently revised Boston criteria for the diagnosis of CAA, enhancing their sensitivity [10,23,51,52].

nodes.description: White-matter rarefaction and loss of axonal or myelin integrity accompany CAA. Diffusion abnormalities correlate with tissue pathology and cognitive performance; the specific mechanisms can include impaired perfusion and other small-vessel injury.

evidence.reference_title: https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/10173198/1/Werring_Pathophysiological%20framework%20for%20CAA%20-%20FINAL.pdf
evidence.snippet: Loss of FA in two white matter tracts (inferior longitudinal fasciculus and anterior thalamic radiation) from 9 sporadic CAA brains was associated with tissue rarefaction and reduced axonal density, and increased MD was associated with reduced myelin density.
